prompt: A carpenter has bundles of pre-cut boards. Which set of three lengths (in feet) could NOT be joined end to end to form a triangle?
hint: The two shorter boards have to reach across the longest one.

hints.text: The two shorter boards have to reach across the longest one.
Triangle Inequality: the two shorter lengths must add to MORE than the longest.
For choice A, $4 + 5 = 9$, which only equals the longest board — the triangle flattens instead of closing.

explanation: The Triangle Inequality says the sum of any two sides must be GREATER than the third.
Check each set with its two shortest boards: $6 + 8 = 14 > 10$ ✓, $7 + 7 = 14 > 7$ ✓, $5 + 9 = 14 > 12$ ✓.
But $4 + 5 = 9$, which is exactly equal to the longest board, not greater. The two short boards lie flat along the long one and enclose no area, so choice A cannot form a triangle.

alternativeExplanations.title: Try to build it
steps: Lay the 9-ft board down. Hinge the 4-ft and 5-ft boards at each end and swing them up to meet.
They only just touch when both are lying flat on the 9-footer. Lift them at all and they come up short — no triangle.
